newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee report basis for new policy -RBI.
newsitem.headline: India rupee report basis for new policy -RBI.

text.p: The report on capital convertibility of the rupee may provide the basis for new policy initiatives by the government, RBI deputy governor Y.V. Reddy told a meeting in Paris on Wednesday.
"In the current situation, one way of assessing the emerging opportunities could be on the basis of the recommendations of the committee," Reddy was quoted as saying in an RBI statement.
"It would be reasonable to expect that it provides a basis for what needs to be done by the authorities in the future."
The RBI statement said Reddy was addressing a seminar at the Adam Smith Institute on the outlook for emerging markets.

"Successful efforts to liberalise capital account in the past have typically been preceded by a strategy of fiscal reforms which significantly reduces the fiscal deficit and finances the remaining deficit with a minimum recourse to inflation tax," Reddy told the seminar.

The panel on capital convertibility earlier this month recommended a reduction in the fiscal deficit to GDP ratio to 3.5 percent by 1999/2000 from the budgeted 4.5 percent in 1997/98 in addition to controlling inflation at 3.0-5.0 percent by 1999/2000.
"This would break the inflationery expectations in India and bring inflation rates in close alignment with international inflation rates," Reddy said.
The committee also called for a sharp reduction in non-performing assets (NPAs) of banks.
"Quite clearly, the load of a high level of NPAs cannot be borne by the banks if the financial system is opened up fully to the forces of competition."
